name: Creality Falcon2 12W
tagline: Entry Creality diode — simple upgrade path for 3D printer owners
tldr: The base Falcon2 12W is Creality's affordable open-frame diode. Less power than Falcon2 Pro but easier on budget. Good for engraving-first users who already trust Creality from 3D printing. Not a cutting powerhouse.
mainObjective: High-quality hobby and light-business engraving with light, slow cutting

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Entry Creality diode — simple upgrade path for 3D printer owners
Open-frame layout — laser glasses and ventilation are your responsibility
Work area 400 × 415 mm on this chassis
12W on Creality Falcon2: engraving-first — photo fills and leather at moderate speeds
Reference engrave job on this module: ~17–26 min
Reference cut job on this module: ~9–15 min
cons: This module targets thin cuts (about 5 mm basswood class) — not thick production plywood
Higher modules in this line (22W) add cut speed and depth
Not the SKU for a shop cutting 5 mm+ stock all day
Open frame: kids, pets, and smoke are not contained
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 12W module on Creality Falcon2. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Run material test grids at engraving speeds first. Add air assist for light cuts. If cut jobs exceed ~30% of your week, open the higher-watt profile on this site and compare times.
